name: Samsara
business_model: Subscription Connected Operations Cloud that combines IoT devices (vehicle gateways, cameras, asset tags) with SaaS for fleet, safety, equipment and workflow management.
overview: Samsara sells an IoT-plus-SaaS platform for physical operations such as fleets, field service and equipment. It reported $1.89B ending ARR for fiscal 2026 (up 30%) and says more than 25 trillion data points flow through its platform annually. Its Data Platform team moves petabytes from RDS, DynamoDB and internal APIs into a Delta Lake on S3 processed with Spark/Databricks. In 2026 it launched AI agents (AI Safety Coach) and Agent Studio for building custom operational agents.

buying_signals.title: Data volume growth to 25T+ data points per year
buying_signals.detail: Samsara says more than 25 trillion data points flow through its platform annually and frames this data asset as the basis of its AI strategy. High-volume IoT telemetry with customer-facing dashboards is a core SingleStore ingest-plus-analytics pattern.

buying_signals.title: AI agents with knowledge bases launched
buying_signals.detail: Agent Studio lets customers attach policies and documents as a knowledge base and build agents over operational data. This suggests retrieval over documents combined with live telemetry; the underlying retrieval stack is not public.

buying_signals.title: Separate OLTP and lakehouse estates
buying_signals.detail: Data flows from RDS and DynamoDB through ingestion/replication systems into Delta Lake for Spark/Databricks processing, indicating data movement between operational and analytical tiers.

buying_signals.title: Strong growth and profitability
buying_signals.detail: 30% ARR growth, record $1M+ deals and second straight GAAP-profitable quarter suggest capacity to invest in platform.

initiatives.title: Petabyte-scale lakehouse ingestion

architectural_fit.rationale: RDS + DynamoDB operational stores replicated into a Databricks/Delta lakehouse is a multi-engine architecture with data movement between tiers.

buying_signals.rationale: Clear AI-agent launch and rapid data growth, but no public statement of latency, cost or pipeline pain.

workload_relevance.rationale: Trillions of time-stamped IoT events per year feeding customer-facing dashboards and agents is a strong match for high-ingest real-time analytics plus vector/full-text retrieval.

organizational_fit.rationale: Public, profitable, ~4,000 employees with a dedicated Data Platform team; Databricks appears entrenched for lakehouse work.

evidence_confidence.rationale: Strong first-party press releases (2026) for scale and AI; architecture detail only from a 2025 job posting; no engineering blog detail on the serving/query layer.

verified_facts.fact: Samsara ended fiscal 2026 with $1.89B ARR, up 30% year over year.
More than 25 trillion data points flow through the Samsara platform annually.
Samsara launched Agent Studio on 2026-06-24, letting customers build AI agents with templates and document knowledge bases.
Samsara's Data Platform ingests from RDS, DynamoDB and internal APIs into Delta Lake on S3 processed with Spark/Databricks.
A 2025 Samsara job posting cites 2.3M+ IoT devices deployed and about 4,000 employees.

inferences.inference: Agent Studio knowledge bases imply a document retrieval layer (likely embeddings and/or keyword search); the specific technology is unknown.
Replicating RDS and DynamoDB into a lakehouse implies latency between operational events and analytical availability for some workloads.
Databricks is likely entrenched for batch and ML, so SingleStore would complement rather than replace it.

discovery_questions: What serves the real-time views customers see in the dashboard today, and how does it relate to the Delta Lake estate?
How do Agent Studio agents retrieve knowledge-base documents and live asset state, and how many systems are involved?
What is the lag between an event landing in RDS/DynamoDB and being queryable for analytics?
As data points grow past 25T per year, which parts of the stack scale cost fastest?
Which agent use cases need sub-second answers over combined telemetry and documents?
opportunity_hypothesis: Hypothesis to validate: Samsara's 25T+ annual data points, split between RDS/DynamoDB operational stores and a Databricks lakehouse, plus new Agent Studio knowledge-base agents, may create demand for a low-latency serving layer that combines fresh telemetry with vector and full-text retrieval. SingleStore would most plausibly complement Databricks as the real-time serving and agent-context tier, not replace it.

outreach.subject: 25T data points and Agent Studio
outreach.body: Hi - Samsara's FY26 release mentions more than 25 trillion data points flowing through the platform each year, and Agent Studio now lets customers ground agents in their own documents. I'm curious how your team serves that mix of live telemetry and document context today alongside the Delta Lake estate. SingleStore is a SQL database that handles high-rate ingest, real-time analytics, and vector plus full-text search in one engine, which some teams use as a serving layer next to Databricks. Open to a short call to compare notes on whether that is relevant for you?
